title: It's Perfectly Normal: Changing Bodies, Growing Up, Sex, and Sexual Health
author: Robie Harris
current_text: In 1996, It's Perfectly Normal: Changing Bodies, Growing Up, Sex, and Sexual Health was challenged in Washington on the stated grounds that it encouraged children to desire sexual gratification and was an example of child pornography. In 2005, a parent challenged It's Perfectly Normal: Changing Bodies, Growing Up, Sex, and Sexual Health as sexually explicit at the Holt Middle School parent library in Fayetteville, AR, but the book was retained. It's Perfectly Normal: Changing Bodies, Growing Up, Sex, and Sexual Health was removed from school district library shelves in Clover Park, Washington. A group of residents unsuccessfully challenged It's Perfectly Normal: Changing Bodies, Growing Up, Sex, and Sexual Health in Charlestown, Pennsylvania, asking that it be removed from the children’s section at Chester County Public Library because they called it an example of child pornography.

sources.quote: In 1996, it was challenged in Washington because the “book is an act of encouragement for children to begin desiring sexual gratification... and is a clear example of child pornography."
sources.title: Robie H. Harris on Life on the Banned Books List | Kirkus Reviews

sources.quote: “It’s Perfectly Normal: Changing Bodies, Growing Up, Sex, and Sexual Health” was published in 1994 and has faced intense criticism for its frank discussions and illustrations of the changes young people experience during puberty. In 2005, it was challenged but retained at the Holt Middle School parent library in Fayetteville, AR, despite a parent’s complaint that it was sexually explicit.
